items.name: md3
items.title: MD3 colours
items.description: The pmndrs Material Design 3 colour layer: the seed config, the package's Tailwind @theme mapping, and the shadcn remap. Additive to the stock shadcn tokens — blocks use `bg-primary` by default and reach for `bg-surface-dim` only where shadcn has no equivalent.
items.author: pmndrs
items.docs:
The CLI cannot touch your root layout, so mount the theme yourself — nothing renders until you do.

Client (simplest):

```tsx
import { Mtb } from 'material-theme-builder/react'
import { pmndrsMtb } from '@/lib/md3'

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body>
        <Mtb {...pmndrsMtb}>{children}</Mtb>
      </body>
    </html>
  )
}
```

Server (no client JS): `<Mtb>` is the only thing carrying `'use client'`, so from an RSC you can call `builder` and emit the CSS yourself.

```tsx
import { builder } from 'material-theme-builder'
import { pmndrsMtb } from '@/lib/md3'

const { source, ...rest } = pmndrsMtb
const css = builder(source, rest).toCss()
// <style dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: css }} /> in <head>
```

With `next-themes`, nest `<ThemeProvider>` inside the theme, not around it.

Two things to know:

- The `:root, .dark` block this item writes must stay **after** the stock `:root {}` / `.dark {}` blocks — that combined selector is what delegates light/dark to MD3 re-emitting its variables rather than to the `.dark` class. If you run `shadcn apply <preset>` later, re-check that ordering survived.
- Reseed per deployment with `THEME_PRIMARY`, `THEME_SCHEME` and `THEME_CONTRAST`. The seed moves the colours; the preset does not.
- Need a colour M3 has no role for? Spread `pmndrsMtb` into your own config and add `customColors` there, rather than editing the installed file. `blend: true` harmonizes them against the pmndrs seed. Then write the four `@theme` lines each one needs yourself — `--color-x`, `--color-on-x`, `--color-x-container`, `--color-on-x-container`. The package's mapping covers standard M3 roles only, and a missing line means Tailwind emits no rule for `bg-x-container` at all, with no error.
